simple.meaning: מַעֲרָב (maʻărâb) is a Hebrew action word meaning “traffic ; by implication, mercantile goods.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 9 times in Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 27:9. The surrounding contexts include family line, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲרָב (H4627) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מַעֲרָב (maʻărâb) / H4627 is traced through Ezekiel 27:9, Ezekiel 27:13, Ezekiel 27:17, Ezekiel 27:19 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4627. maarab I. [ מַעֲרָב ] noun masculine usually collective articles of exchange, merchandise (only of Tyre, Ezekiel 27); — suffix מַעֲרָבֵךְ Job 17:13 ; Job 17:17; Job 17:19; Job 17:25; Job 17:27a; Job 17:34; as accusative of congnate meaning with verb with עָרַב 17:9 ; Job 17:27; plural suffix מַעֲרָבַיִךְ Job 17:33 perhaps thy (diverse) wares (DHM VOJ viii (1894), 4 proposes, ingeniously, meaning imports , deriving from V. ערב enter , but improbable).
